item.title: Explainer-What is ASEAN and why does the bloc matter?
item.description:
By Karen Lema

MANILA, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Major powers have joined a summit of Southeast Asian nations hosted by the Philippines against one of the most complex backdrops for the regional bloc, from the Iran war that has battered economies to the growing US-China rivalry.

Closer to home, the 11 members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations are grappling with a crisis in civil war-torn Myanmar, conflict between Thailand and Cambodia, and tension over competing claims in the South China Sea.

Here are five key aspects of the bloc.

item.title: Turkey appoints trustee to pro-opposition TV channel Sozcu, outlet says
item.description:
ANKARA, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Turkish authorities raided the offices of pro-oppositionSozcu TV early on Tuesday and appointed a trustee to run its television and online platforms, the channel said, extending a crackdown on the opposition and renewing concerns about media freedom.

In a statement on its website, Sozcu TV said some of its executives had been detained.

"A new one was added to the operations against newspaper and television channels in Turkey. Police carried out raids against Sozcu TV and Sozcu.com.tr in the morning," the channel said.

item.title: Oman, Iran discuss safeguarding maritime corridors, as attacks in Hormuz increase
item.description:
DUBAI, Nov 17 (Reuters) - Oman and Iran discussed safeguarding maritime corridors and ensuring the smooth flow of global shipping and trade, the Omani foreign ministry said in a statement on Tuesday, as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz continued to be disrupted.

The talks took place during a visit by Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi to Oman, which holds the southern coast of the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route for global energy, and has played a role as mediator in the crisis that broke out when the US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28.

item.title: West Bank's displaced Palestinians hold little hope for post-Netanyahu era
item.description:
After Israeli forces pushed him and thousands of others out of the West Bank refugee camp of Tulkarem last year, Adel Darsieh held onto his hope of returning home, but it is fading fast. 

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed no return for the displaced people from the camp near the northern city of Jenin, known as a hub for militants.

He is now fighting for his political life after his party lost seats in Israel's general election last month and former general Gadi Eisenkot was tasked with trying to form a new government.

item.title: 'I cannot forget': Yazidi genocide survivors testify at 'truth commission'
item.description:
Ardawan Abdi was just 14 when Islamic State (IS) group jihadists seized the ancestral homeland of his Yazidi people in northern Iraq's Sinjar Mountains and locked him up for seven months. 

"In that time, I saw everything, from blood to death," he told AFP in Berlin on Monday on the sidelines of a first-of-its-kind "truth commission" for survivors of the Yazidi genocide that started in 2014.
